clue.text: Film editor cited poor crits hammered, i.e. rejected (12, two words)

the abbreviation's two letters, to be taken out

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I and E from the fourteen letters, then rearrange the twelve left.
explanation.definitionFit: A script doctor is a writer hired to revise and improve a screenplay, an editor of the film's text.

clue.text: Stopper

explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a bung or stopple that seals a hole, such as a bath's drain.

clue.text: Wealthy Springbok (not Habana) nearly ruined

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Larney is South African slang for a rich, often white, person, or for something smart and posh.

clue.text: Amulet in metal is man-made

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, running across their word breaks

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A lucky charm made of artificial metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck or ward off harm, the same thing as an amulet.

clue.text: Lacking bit at the end/, like a disgruntled waiter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without a point or end piece

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of tip, a pointed end and a gratuity, give the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipless describes anything missing its end piece, and a waiter left no gratuity would be justly fed up.

clue.text: What gets Hindu trembling with fear — this fiend?

definitions.text: What gets Hindu trembling with fear — this fiend?

indicators.note: trembling things shake and jumble, so the letters are rearranged
the answer is what you get from the mix once the final named word is set aside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word itself, which joins the answer in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Which demon makes a Hindu shake with terror?
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with the clue's last word rearranges to the two words before the indicator. Rahu is the demon of Hindu myth who swallows the sun or moon, causing eclipses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rahu is a demon in Hindu mythology, so it is just the kind of fiend a believer would dread.

clue.text: Pointed bean appearing before end of July

explanation.walkthrough: Urdy is a heraldic term, as in a cross urdy.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry urdy describes a line or cross with pointed, spiky projections.

clue.text: Are they pointless? Not quite, or not at all

definitions.text: Are they pointless? Not quite, or not at all

indicators.note: not quite complete means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: needless means having no point, unnecessary

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether some things lack a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is NEEDLESS, and not quite that drops the last S; the clue then answers itself, since needles are anything but pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are sharp slender pins, so they are the very opposite of pointless, which the closing phrase states.

clue.text: Crowning garlands worn irk eye badly in part of mass (12, two words)

done badly means put together wrongly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the two words taken as written
leis are Hawaiian flower garlands
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Wearing a garland of flowers on the head irritates the eye during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie eleison, 'Lord, have mercy', is a fixed prayer near the start of the Mass.

clue.text: Streaks in coal? Could be such sets, OK, when mined

the words themselves, which join the answer in the rearrangement

clue.text: Pale, like a gannet that's deprived of half feed

the second half of the four-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gannet is a greedy person, from the seabird's appetite; take ED out of the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes a pallid, washed-out complexion, as in looking grey with illness.

the same abbreviation again

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the ruru is better known in New Zealand; it is the boobook owl, also found in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruru is the boobook or morepork, a small owl of New Zealand and Australia.

clue.text: Edrich batting, a combative fellow of old

explanation.walkthrough: John and Bill Edrich were England Test batsmen, which makes 'batting' read as cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A chider is one who scolds or quarrels, an old word for a contentious person.

clue.text: Endlessly senseless hullabaloo ensuring good breeding?

indicators.note: with no end, the next word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Pointless constant fuss over making sure one is well brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is ironic: in-and-in breeding means repeated mating of close relatives, which may fix a pedigree but is hardly good breeding in the social sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In-and-in describes breeding from closely related stock, done to fix desirable traits in a line.

clue.text: Less hard work than a hammer? See chippy align one (7, two words)

definitions.text: Less hard work than a hammer?

'un is a dialect form of one

explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for a carpenter, which makes it look like part of the scene rather than the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail gun drives nails mechanically, so it takes far less effort than swinging a hammer.

clue.text: Rule circumvented by a copper keeping in line

R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side in a line, as when marching or walking level.

clue.text: Commoner section of people believe (giving his word contentiously!)

explanation.surface: A political row over whether someone used a sneering word about ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket recalls the 2012 Plebgate row, when a British minister was accused of calling police officers plebs and denied using the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleb, short for plebeian, is an ordinary person of low social rank.

clue.text: Object in fur that can be shipped

explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female dancer, especially in ballet, which is what a ballerina is.

clue.text: Crafty poems about 'do' (as it was called)

ut was the old name for the first note of the scale, now do

explanation.walkthrough: In sol-fa, the note now sung as do was once called ut.
explanation.definitionFit: Versute is an archaic word for cunning or wily, from the Latin for adroit.

clue.text: Not seated? That may be disturbing to one

the word itself, which joins the answer in the rearrangement

explanation.definitionFit: A standee is someone who stands, as on a crowded train or at a show, because no seat is free.
